scenes.caption: Buying an RV means 30 dealer sites describing the same trailer 30 different ways. On real dealer pages, GVWR is machine-readable under 1% of the time. Agents can't shop on that web.
MatchRV fixes the layer underneath: this page exposes its real inventory as ten structured WebMCP tools — capabilities, not a chatbot.
One messy sentence in — F-150, two kids, bunkhouse trailer under $45k, under 30 ft, near Tacoma, we boondock, solar & lithium — and the agent calls search_inventory with typed constraints.
1,056 real units searched in ~15 ms. Same results on the page and in the agent — and the funnel says exactly what was excluded, and why.
The tow question is answered honestly: a bare “F-150” is a 5,000–13,500 lb range, so the rail states the range and asks for the door-sticker rating instead of guessing.

Every recommendation carries receipts: which hard checks passed on verified data, the exact score math, and what is unknown — solar the dealer never published stays a question mark. Unknown is not no.
Shared state, both directions. The human clicks a preference by hand — two entry doors — and it lands in the same session the agent reads.
“Drop the budget to $35k.” The agent's next call is a refine: everything else is kept, the whole funnel recomputes, and the ledger shows You, then Agent.
compare_units returns true values, not prose — best-in-row markers, tow margins spelled out, and unknown cells left visibly Unknown. The agent reasons over real numbers.

Now the consequential part. The agent can only stage a dealer contact: here is exactly what would be sent, behind a literal NOT SENT banner. The message it drafted asks the dealer to confirm the unknowns.
If the agent tries to submit early, the server refuses. Approval is a single-use token only this page holds — never in any tool result, never in the model's context.
The human clicks Approve. Now it goes through — once.
An exact receipt: dealer, unit, time, reference. Duplicates are blocked. And it never claims a real dealership was contacted — this is a demo environment, and it says so.
